summary:
THE LAST SIGNAL: Echoes of Exploration is an interactive digital platform, investigative archive, and educational presentation developed by Team LORE. The project is designed to bridge the gap between complex software engineering methodologies and the captivating history of space exploration, transforming raw telemetry and mission logs into an accessible, engaging experience for students and young learners.  
Core Vision & Purpose
Rather than presenting space history as a collection of static dates and technical jargon, The Last Signal focuses on the "forgotten side" of exploration: the resilient spacecraft, rovers, and landers left operating in extreme environments long after their primary missions end. Under the guiding theme "Every mission ends. Its discoveries do not," the project demonstrates how lost or dormant signals can be reconstructed, analyzed, and preserved as an enduring scientific legacy.  
Key Components & Interactive Experience
Mission Control & Data Investigation: The platform invites users to step into the role of a space investigator. Through an interactive interface, visitors examine simulated logs, trace signal waveforms, and analyze critical system decisions—moving from passive reading to active problem-solving.  
Historic Mission Spotlights: The archive highlights three landmark space missions—Opportunity (the Mars rover that operated for over 15 years), Apollo 11 (humanity’s historic first steps on the Moon)

THE LAST SIGNAL — Echoes of Exploration

The Last Signal is an interactive, web-based educational investigation game that transforms real NASA space missions into immersive stories, allowing players to explore scientific discoveries through evidence, mission records, and interactive storytelling.

The Problem

NASA provides enormous amounts of valuable scientific data, images, and mission records. However, this information can be difficult for students and non-specialists to navigate and understand.

The challenge is not a lack of information, but the gap between scientific data and public understanding.

Our Solution

The Last Signal bridges this gap by combining scientific exploration with interactive storytelling.

Players explore real space missions through three connected experiences:

  • Mission Archives: Explore NASA imagery, historical records, scientific observations, mission timelines, and illustrated educational stories.
  • Interactive Investigation: Examine mission files, collect evidence, analyze information, and understand the scientific and engineering challenges behind each mission.
  • Visual Storytelling: Experience complex space exploration concepts through accessible narratives and illustrated content.

Our project currently features three NASA mission themes:

Opportunity: Explore the Mars rover's scientific achievements, its search for evidence of past water, and the 2018 dust storm that ended communication.

InSight: Discover how seismic measurements and scientific instruments helped researchers investigate the interior of Mars.

Apollo: Explore historical lunar missions through mission records, photographs, and educational storytelling.

The Opportunity mission includes a playable investigation experience, while InSight and Apollo are represented through their scientific archives.

Technologies and Development

We developed The Last Signal as a browser-based interactive experience using:

  • Next.js and React: Web application architecture and interactive interfaces.
  • TypeScript: Application logic and structured development.
  • Tailwind CSS: Responsive interface design.
  • NASA and JPL resources: Scientific information, mission images, and historical references.
  • GitHub: Source-code management and collaboration.
  • Vercel: Web application deployment.
  • AI-assisted creative and development tools: Supporting visual design, content preparation, and implementation.

We chose web technologies rather than a traditional game engine to make the experience accessible through a browser and to focus development effort on scientific content, interaction, and user experience.

Creativity and Innovation

Our approach combines real scientific records, narrative-driven exploration, illustrated educational content, and interactive investigation.

Instead of simply presenting NASA information in a conventional educational website, we invite users to discover the stories behind the missions.

We also distinguish documented scientific facts from fictional narrative elements to support responsible science communication.

Intended Impact and Future Development

Our goal is to make space science more approachable, especially for students, young learners, and people without specialized scientific backgrounds.

We hope to inspire curiosity, encourage exploration of NASA's original resources, and help users understand how scientific discoveries emerge from mission evidence.

Future development will focus on expanding playable investigations to additional missions, improving accessibility and multilingual support, and evaluating learning outcomes through structured user testing.

The Last Signal transforms space exploration from information to experience.
